chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Beware of joking, for it removes the water (dignity) of the face and the sublimity of the men.

key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Water of the face, a metaphor for dignity and composure
key_terms.مَهَابَةِ الرِّجَالِ: Sublimity or awe of the men, referring to respect and reverence

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social consequence of excessive joking in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against frivolous joking (al-mizah), noting that it erodes 'water of the face'—a metaphor for the luminous dignity and composure of the self—and diminishes the awe (mahabah) others hold for you. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and *wajihah* (dignified presence), where excessive laughter is seen as a loss of spiritual gravity. The advice aligns with the broader ethical framework of balancing joy with solemnity to maintain one's status as a leader or scholar.
